purpose: Replace the fictional service-provider catalog and client-supplied compliance facts with a tenant-scoped PostgreSQL Provider, ProviderCapability, ServiceOffering and server-held evidence authority.
requiredInvariants: Provider, ProviderCapability, ServiceOffering and compliance evidence are PostgreSQL-authoritative and tenant-scoped.
The static pilot catalog, fictional provider identities, default bank and client-supplied evidence authority are removed.
Organization, tenant, membership and provider ownership are derived server-side.
Organization administrators may self-declare provider capabilities and offerings only into PENDING_VERIFICATION; they cannot create LIVE_OK evidence or activate themselves.
PostgreSQL FORCE RLS denies cross-tenant access and same-tenant outsider mutation.
CAS versioning, advisory serialization and payload-bound idempotency protect every mutation.
Provider mutation, append-only event, chained audit and outbox rows commit in one transaction.
Catalog, recommendation, plan and compliance responses use only durable server-held rows.
No provider backfill, default provider, downstream Deal enforcement, paid dependency or external partner access is introduced.
acceptance: An organization administrator can declare a capability only after declaring the mapped OrganizationCapability.
An organization administrator can create or withdraw an offering without selecting authority fields.
Self-declared provider capabilities and offerings remain PENDING_VERIFICATION and are excluded from the active catalog.
Compliance ignores all client evidence fields and evaluates only stored registry evidence.
Exact replay returns the original receipt and a changed payload under the same key is rejected.
Concurrent commands using the same expected version produce one commit and one stale-version result.
A forced audit or outbox failure rolls back provider state and the append-only event.
The scope guard confirms no registration or role-eligibility path changed.
